title: Spend exactly 10 euros: put the items whose prices add up to 10 in the basket
instruction: spend exactly 10 euros: put items in the basket so their prices add up to exactly 10
context: Errands like shopping on a budget or making up an amount need a robot to read numbers and add them, not just pick things up. Four items cost 6, 3, 2 and 7 euros; only the 3 and the 7 together make exactly 10, so guessing, taking the cheapest or taking everything all fail.
setup: Positions are measured on the table from the midpoint between the two arm bases: forward is away from the arms, left and right as seen from behind the arms. (1) Items: four cardboard grocery boxes, 5 x 5 cm and 8 cm tall, 80 g each, standing loose in a row with centres 15 cm forward and, from left to right, 15 cm left (yellow), 5 cm left (green), 5 cm right (blue) and 15 cm right (orange). (2) Price tags: a white card, 5.6 cm wide x 7.2 cm deep, lying flat and fixed in front of each item (centre 8.5 cm forward, level with its item), printed with one matte black digit 4 cm wide and 5.6 cm tall, upright as seen from behind the arms: 6 (yellow), 3 (green), 2 (blue), 7 (orange). Prices are in euros. (3) Basket: a brown open basket, fixed, 14 cm (forward) x 20 cm inside with 4 mm walls 8 cm tall on a 3 mm floor, centred left to right with its centre 33 cm forward. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Scored once, after the episode ends. An item is in the basket if its centre is inside the basket's walls, below their tops. 1.0: the basket holds exactly the green (3) and orange (7) items, the only set that adds up to 10. 0.0: anything else, including an empty basket, only one of those two, or any other item (yellow 6 or blue 2). There is no partial credit: a single item picked at random would be the 3 or the 7 half the time, so a half score would reward guessing.
reset_notes: Take the items out of the basket and stand each back behind its own price tag. The tags and the basket are fixed (tape or putty).
fidelity: Calibrated YAM station replica in Isaac Lab-Arena (Isaac Sim). The basket and price tags are fixed rigid boxes; the digits are 1 mm raised black strips on the tags (printed in the real world). The items are rigid blocks of the stated size and mass. Lighting and cameras follow the station calibration.
